aspects.says: A composite field is a row of datasets, each a one-byte identifier, a two-byte big-endian length counting its content, and the content; the field prefix, dataset lengths and TLV lengths must agree.
basis: section:17.1. A Composite Field Is a Row of Datasets, and Each Announces Its Own Length

aspects.says: DE 55 is composite but carries raw BER-TLV with no envelope, so a reader must know which fields have one.
basis: section:17.3. DE 55 Is Composite but Has No Envelope

aspects.says: A field number means something only with its edition, so a switch maps between 1987 and 2023 links through its internal format and passes DE 55 through unchanged.
basis: section:17.7. The Same Field Number Means Different Things on a 1987 Link and a 2023 Link

aspects.says: Identifiers 01-70 are TLV datasets and 71-FE bitmap datasets, 00 and FF are invalid; an unknown dataset can be stepped over but a bitmap dataset's elements need the field's definition.
basis: section:17.2. The Identifier's Range Says How to Read a Dataset, and Only the Field's Definition Says What It Holds

aspects.says: A path names one element at one level: after DE 55 comes a tag, after another field a dataset, then a tag only inside a TLV dataset; absent is not an error.
basis: section:17.5. A Path Names One Element at One Level

aspects.says: A reader walks the envelopes from the start, steps over unknown datasets by their length, and refuses overruns and the bytes 00 and FF.
basis: section:17.4. A Reader Walks the Envelopes, Steps Over What It Doesn't Know and Refuses What Overruns

aspects.says: The writer encodes every length itself: BER long forms from 128 bytes, a two-byte dataset length up to 65535, and no TLVList.pack() with its 516-byte buffer.
basis: section:17.6. A Writer Encodes Every Length Itself, Because the Packager Sees Only Bytes
